text:
incident-bot: [ALERT] CRITICAL - GPU pool `spot-usw2-gpu` at 95% utilization. Queue length: ~1.8k requests. Autoscaler reported 5 failed allocation attempts in the last 10m. Latency SLO for /generation exceeded (p95 > 800ms). Pager: #oncall

mia: ack, taking this. oncall-ingress.

mia: quick triage: running autoscaler logs for last 10m
mia: ``/ops/autoscaler logs --pool spot-usw2-gpu --since 10m`` shows repeated `AllocationError: quotaExceeded` and `InsufficientCapacityError: NotEnoughInstances` from cloud provider.

carla: confirmed spike in queued tokens for prod /generation route, looks correlated with two customers sending long-batch jobs around 02:10 UTC.

mia: can we enable the dedicated-fallback? current pool policy had `fallback_to_dedicated: false`.

dinesh: i'm on infra. flipping fallback to true now, will also request +4 dedicated nodes from reserved pools.
dinesh: applying change:
```yaml
pool: spot-usw2-gpu
fallback_to_dedicated: true
max_fallback_nodes: 8
```

sre-bot: runbook "spot-pool-fallback" triggered by mia. Steps: enable fallback, throttle low-priority routes, request dedicated nodes, notify CS. Link: https://runbooks.internal/spot-pool-fallback

mia: while we wait for nodes, throttling non-critical routes and reducing burst windows. Pushing config: `/config/routes/prod-throttle` -> set low-priority token rate to 0.2 rps.

carla: also switching heavy workloads from `redwood-7b` to `redwood-7b-quant` for now to reduce memory pressure — doing a controlled route rewrite for 10% traffic then 100% for affected customers.

raj: paging cloud-support, opening case for InsufficientCapacity in us-west-2, asking for expedited capacity or suggestions for different instance types. Case #CS-98765 created.

emily: CS is drafting incident banner and targeted notices for the 3 affected customers. ETA 10m.

mia: autoscaler returned an error stack snippet: ``AllocationError: QuotaExceeded: Requested 4 GPUs, available quota 0.\n at provider.allocate (/ops/providers/aws.go:412)\n CausedBy: InsufficientCapacityError: NotEnoughInstances``

dinesh: manual request for dedicated nodes submitted: `./infra/scale.sh --pool dedicated-usw2-gpu --add 4` -> pending. If cloud cannot fulfill, we'll spin up mixed-instance types from warm-pool.

mia: temporary mitigation summary applied: fallback enabled, low-priority throttles set, model fallback to quantized variants, +4 dedicated nodes requested. Monitoring queue length now.

(3m later)

incident-bot: Update: dedicated node request acknowledged by infra; cloud support replied with suggested alternate instance types (a100 -> a10x). Trying warm-pool spin-up. Queue length dropped to 860. p95 latency now ~420ms.

carla: customer X job still in queue, moving their requests to dedicated-capacity route; doing an on-the-fly route override.

mia: leaving detailed notes in the runbook and handing off to raj for monitoring and follow-ups in next 20m. My shift ends in 25m.

raj: ack, taking over. Will keep the runbook open and continue escalation if warm-pool doesn't stabilize. I'll also check billing/limits and coordinate with sales for customers impacted if SLA credits needed.

sre-bot: Incident state updated to "mitigated" (partial). Actions applied: fallback enabled, throttles active, 4 dedicated nodes requested. Next steps: confirm full capacity, postmortem cadence, CS notifications.

emily: posting customer notices now. will include mitigation summary and expected follow-up.

mia: final note before handoff: add `model-fallback` test to nightly evals to avoid regressions when we auto-route to quantized models.

raj: thanks. I'll keep monitoring and will escalate to oncall-manager if queue climbs above 1k again.

incident-bot: Thread closed for now (participants: mia, dinesh, carla, raj, emily).
